item.title: Iran's supreme leader issues his first statement as war with U.S. and Israel rages
item.summary: Iran's state media broadcast what it said was a public statement by Mojtaba Khamenei, as Day 13 of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran rages.

item.title: Trump's war with Iran is angering some swing voters who want money spent at home
item.summary: Swing voters who helped reelect President Trump in 2024 don't support his decision to go to war in Iran and instead want to see U.S. tax dollars spent tackling economic pressures facing Americans.

item.title: Chilean Smiljan Radić Clarke wins architecture's highest honor
item.summary: The Pritzker Prize was awarded Thursday. "In every work, he is able to answer with radical originality, making the unobvious obvious," said fellow Chilean architect and prize chair Alejandro Aravena.

item.title: The Trump administration's crackdown on immigrant truckers shifts into higher gear
item.summary: The White House wants tougher rules for commercial licenses after several high-profile crashes involving foreign-born drivers. But critics say that would do little to make the nation's roads safer.

item.title: Easy-to-use solar panels are coming, but utilities are trying to delay them
item.summary: Utilities are convincing lawmakers around the U.S. to delay bills that would allow people to buy solar panels, plug them into an outlet and begin generating electricity.

item.title: El Niño is set to take hold this summer, driving up global temperatures
item.summary: A potentially strong El Niño weather pattern will likely emerge this summer and persist through the rest of the year. The hottest years on record generally occur in years when El Niño is active.

item.title: 'Songs from the Hole': The story behind JJ'88's documentary and visual album
item.summary: The visual album and documentary Songs from the Hole tells the story of James Jacobs, the hip-hop artist JJ'88, as he reflects on his coming-of-age within California's state prison system.

item.title: 5 ways to resist the urge to keep looking at your phone
item.summary: So you want to spend less time on your phone. How do you do that when it's designed to suck you in? Life Kit spoke to experts in behavioral science, psychology and technology for real-world advice.

item.title: Rep. Kevin Kiley talks about why he switched his party affiliation
item.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with Rep. Kevin Kiley of California about changing his political party affiliation from Republican to Independent.

item.title: Bam Adebayo's 83-point night was one to remember. But not everyone was pleased
item.summary: Detractors point to Adebayo's one-of-a-kind stat line — 43 field goal attempts, 22 3-point attempts and, most of all, NBA records of 36 free throws and 43 attempts — as proof of stat-padding.
